findings.problem:
The proof of spin_hfam has the same two-stage skeleton as sp_hfam and sl_hfam in RankTwoCoverSpMain.lean and RankTwoCoverSLMain.lean.

Stage 1: destructure the 14-component witness tuple from `*_orth` and feed it, name by name, into `orthSep_of_noConj h hinj hH (…_card_rankOne …) (fun k => hasOrderThree_data (hasSL2Node_… k).hasOrderThree) …`. The plumbing is identical in all three files. Only the family-specific inputs differ: the orth lemma, the card lemma and the SL2 node.

Stage 2: after `exists_pair_of_three a b c P …` and `refine ⟨i, j, ?_, hcol, hP⟩`, each file discharges `i ≠ j` with `rcases hij with ⟨rfl, rfl⟩ | ⟨rfl, rfl⟩ | ⟨rfl, rfl⟩ <;> simp [Fin.ext_iff, a, b, c]`, plus `<;> omega` in the Spin case. The statement `exists_pair_of_three` is too weak to yield `i ≠ j`, so every caller redoes this case split.

The predicate `fun i j => OrthSep … ∨ ¬ IsPSolvable 3 …` is also restated by hand in the lemma statement and again in the `exists_pair_of_three` call, in all three files.
findings.proposed_change:
Add two lemmas to RankTwoCoverFamilies.lean and RankTwoCoverSep.lean.

1. `exists_ne_pair_of_three {ι} (a b c : ι) (hab : a ≠ b) (hac : a ≠ c) (hbc : b ≠ c) (P : ι → ι → Prop) (h₁ : P a b) (h₂ : P a c) (h₃ : P b c) (col : ι → Bool) : ∃ i j, i ≠ j ∧ col i = col j ∧ P i j`.
   Proof: apply `exists_pair_of_three`, then `rcases` the three-way disjunction and `subst`/`exact` the matching `hab`, `hac` or `hbc`.

2. `orthSep_of_orth_data`, taking `h`, `hinj`, `hH`, `h6`, `h3` and `hij hcart`, with the 14-component existential (`∃ xi ∈ …, … ∧ ∀ k …`) as one hypothesis. Its proof is `obtain ⟨…⟩ := hdata; exact orthSep_of_noConj h hinj hH h6 h3 hij hcart …`.

Rewritten uses:
- In spin_hfam, `horth` becomes `fun i j hij hcart => orthSep_of_orth_data h hinj hH (spin_card_rankOne hF hn3) (fun k => hasOrderThree_data (hasSL2Node_spinPlus (F := F) hn3 k).hasOrderThree) hij hcart (spin_orth hF hn3 i j hij hcart)`.
- The tail becomes `obtain ⟨i, j, hne, hcol, hP⟩ := exists_ne_pair_of_three a b c hab' hac' hbc' _ (Or.inl hab) (Or.inl hac) (Or.inl hbc) col; exact ⟨i, j, hne, hcol, hP⟩`. The three `a ≠ b`, `a ≠ c`, `b ≠ c` proofs already appear inline as the `fun h => by have := congrArg Fin.val h; …` arguments to `horth`, so they can be named once and reused.
- sp_hfam and sl_hfam use the same two lemmas. sp_hfam passes `sp_orth (i := a) (j := c) hF …` and sl_hfam passes `sl_orth hF a c …`.
- Optionally add a `def`/`abbrev` for the predicate `OrthSep D π i j ∨ ¬ IsPSolvable 3 ↥((rankOne … i ⊔ rankOne … j).map π)`, so each hfam statement and its `P` argument can use it.
findings.benefit: The Stage 1 and Stage 2 logic, including the fiddly case split on which pair was chosen, is written once and tested once instead of three times in the Spin, Sp and SL files. Each `*_hfam` proof then shows only what is family-specific: the choice of three indices, their Cartan/adjacency facts, and the orth and card lemmas. A future change to `orthSep_of_noConj` or `OrthSep` needs one edit instead of three parallel edits. The Spin proof also drops its `<;> omega` workaround after the `rcases`.
